messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: NuVision call recap — data handling checklist + next steps

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps. I captured the asks and a proposed exception path that should unblock procurement while we finalize contract language.

Key points from today (NuVision):
- Primary concern: patient-identifiable PII must not be retained in a way that allows re-identification.
- Preference: 0-retention for PHI fields; if not possible, shortest feasible TTL (customer suggested 3-7 days) with cryptographic protections.
- Debugging/support: NuVision needs assurances that support engineers cannot access raw PII; they are open to redaction + encrypted logs if that meets control requirements.
- Residency: data must be processed in US region; they may evaluate Private deployment if controls require.

Proposed exception path (what we can offer quickly):
1) Short-log pilot: 7-day KV/prefix logs with automatic redaction rules for recognized PHI patterns + API-level opt-out for specific routes (e.g., doctor-note ingestion).
2) Encryption & access controls: logs encrypted at rest, access via audited role-based access; support access only via break-glass with approval and audit trail.
3) Evidence: provide SOC 2 Type II audit excerpts and a short control mapping doc.
4) Contractual addendum: narrow carveout clause that defines the shortened retention window and limitations; formalized by an amendment/DocuSign.

Requested deliverables (next 72 hours):
- From NuVision: filled privacy checklist you sent (I attached our copy to this thread).
- From Redwood: SOC 2 excerpt + proposed amendment language + quick quote on pricing impact for short-log retention + timeline for an optional Private pilot.

I attached: NuVision_Privacy_Checklist_filled.pdf (your completed checklist) and I'll follow up with draft amendment and control mapping tomorrow.

Next steps (owners):
- Marissa: pricing impact and commercial note (ETA Tue).
- Ben: collect SOC2 excerpt + engineering contact for redaction/KV plan (ETA Mon).
- Stephanie: draft amendment + DocuSign path and coordinate pilot proposal.

Thanks — talk soon.

--

Thanks Stephanie — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side after internal sync:

- NuVision stance: for any field that contains patient identifiers (name, MRN, SSN, DOB when linked to identity), we need near-0 retention. Where possible we prefer 0-retention (no logs persisted).
- Non-identifiable telemetry (latency, token counts, non-PII usage stats) is fine to retain for 30–90 days.
- For debugging: we can accept a model where PII is redacted before persisting and a short TTL applies to redacted traces. However, we need to confirm that redaction is irreversible and that support cannot retrieve raw text.
- On-prem/private: this is a hard requirement only if Redwood cannot demonstrate equivalent technical and contractual controls for 0/short retention.

Open Qs for Redwood:
1) Can you confirm whether redaction rules can be tuned by NuVision (custom patterns) or will Redwood provide only built-in patterns?
2) What is the SLA for break-glass access requests and how are they audited?
3) If we start with a 7-day short-log pilot, what are the commercial credits or pricing differentials?

We filled and attached the checklist as requested. We can review your draft amendment once it's available — Daniel will own legal redlines.

Aisha
Director, Product Security

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the proposed path. From legal's perspective we can accept a time-limited exception if the following are captured explicitly in contract language and technical controls are demonstrable:

1) Narrow scope: list of routes/data types that qualify for short-log handling (e.g., chat ingestion endpoints flagged for PHI).
2) Retention schedule: explicit TTL (7 days) for redacted traces; clause that prohibits reconstitution of redacted content.
3) Access controls: encryption-at-rest, RBAC for support, break-glass procedure with 2-person approval, and full audit trail retained for 1 year.
4) Audit rights: NuVision must be able to request evidence (SOC2 excerpts, access logs) on a quarterly basis; Redwood to provide redacted support access logs within 10 business days.
5) Remedies & termination: if controls are violated, NuVision may terminate and request deletion of customer-derived models/derivatives.

Suggested clause (draft language):
"Redwood may implement a short-log data handling exception limited to the routes and data types explicitly listed in Schedule X. For data types designated as PHI by Customer, Redwood will apply irreversible redaction prior to any persistent storage and will retain redacted traces for no more than seven (7) days. Access to redacted traces is restricted to authorized personnel only and requires dual approval; all access events will be logged and made available to Customer upon request."

Please attach the SOC2 excerpt and the proposed Schedule X. We will review the draft amendment and redlines; if acceptable we can proceed to DocuSign for an amendment signature. Also cc'ing eng-privacy for technical follow-up on redaction irreversibility.

Regards,
Daniel Park
Senior Counsel, NuVision Health
